thread:
Alex C: FYI — incident-bot fired a bunch of pages overnight for `inference-runtime:latency_spike` and PD spun up three incidents. Looks like auto-grouping didn't collapse them. Customers saw elevated 500s briefly. Can we do a quick postmortem and tuning pass on suppression?

incident-bot: ALERT: page_fired service=inference-runtime region=us-west-2 severity=critical count=3 grouping_key=auto-2026-03-13-02

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-98765 - inference-runtime latency spike (escalation: oncall-sre)

Priya R: ugh, saw this in the logs. The grouping key changed per node because the error stacktrace included pid. auto-grouping rule used too-high-cardinality fields.

Jamie L: Confirmed — grouping_key included `host_id` in the payload for the alert rule. The dedupe window was 60s, and because nodes flapped, it created distinct groups.

Alex C: Does the PD surge match any deployment or autoscaling events?

Priya R: Not that I can see. CPU and GPU metrics looked normal. There was a short KV cache miss storm that coincided with a config rollout (2026-03-13 01:58 UTC) but errors were transient.

Jamie L: Proposed quick fixes: 1) Remove host_id from grouping key. 2) Increase dedupe window to 300s for this alert. 3) Add suppression for repeat pages within 5m per customer. Thoughts?

incident-bot: SUGGESTION: auto-suppress threshold currently=5 pages / 60s. Suggested change=3 pages / 300s for service=inference-runtime.

Priya R: +1 on removing host_id. Also suggest enabling `suppress_on_escalation=true` so when PD incident is open we don't create duplicate pages.

Alex C: Agree. We should also add a short-term silence for the noisy alert while we fix rules. Can someone run `pd silence`?

pagerduty-bot: Command received: `pd silence --service inference-runtime --duration 15m --reason "auto-grouping noise"`

pagerduty-bot: Silence applied to service inference-runtime for 15m by Priya R

Jamie L: I'll push the grouping rule change now to staging and then prod if tests pass. Patch: remove `host_id` from `group_by` in alerts.yaml and bump `dedupe_window` to 300s.

Jamie L: (code)
```
alerts:
  - name: inference-runtime-latency
    group_by: [service, region]    # removed host_id
    dedupe_window: 300
    suppress_on_escalation: true
```

Priya R: @Alex C can you validate that PD suppression behavior won't hide real multi-customer outages? We need per-customer page still if ingestion>50% errors.

Alex C: Good point. Keep a high-priority rule that pages immediately when `customer_impact>50%`. Everything else can be deduped. Add `customer_threshold` field.

incident-bot: NOTE: existing historical pages: 2026-03-13T02:01:12Z x3, 02:03:20Z x2 from different nodes. Grouping mismatch count=5.

Jamie L: Rolling the config to prod in 2m. Will monitor for any new PD incidents.

Priya R: After you deploy, can you also bump the auto-suppress threshold from 5->3 for 10m? That should cut down paging storms during transient flaps.

Jamie L: Done in staging. Deploying to prod now.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note: PD-98765 acknowledged by Priya R

Alex C: Thanks. Priya — can you take PD handoff if it escalates? I'll check customer-facing metrics and open a quick postmortem doc.

Priya R: Taking handoff. I'll reach out to affected customers if the PD flips to major incident.

incident-bot: ACTION: created ticket #OPS-4321 to track alert config changes and follow-up postmortem.

Jamie L: Prod changes live. I removed host_id and increased dedupe_window. Also added `suppress_on_escalation=true`.

Priya R: Monitoring dashboards — error rate back to baseline, no new pages in the last 4m. Looks good.

Alex C: Follow-ups: (1) Update runbook to prefer `customer_impact` grouping over host-level; (2) Add unit tests for grouping logic to prevent regression; (3) Schedule a 30-min oncall review to tune thresholds. I'll create calendar invite.

Priya R: +1 on runbook. Also recommend we add a metric for "pages avoided" to measure suppression effectiveness.

Jamie L: Fine by me. I'll add a Grafana panel for suppressed_pages and grouping_mismatch_rate.

Alex C: Thanks all — closing thread. If anything else pops, reopen. :white_check_mark:
